title: Slow Cooker Korean Braised Short Ribs

items: 3–4 lb bone-in English-cut short ribs (2- to 3-inch pieces)
¼ cup mirin (or 3 Tbsp rice vinegar plus 1 Tbsp sugar)
1 small Asian pear, peeled and grated (or 1 apple, grated)
½ cup water or beef broth
3 carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks
1 lb daikon radish, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks (or 1 lb baby potatoes)
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, optional, soaked in hot water 20 min and stemmed
1 Tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 Tbsp cold water, optional

steps: Put the ribs in a large pot, cover with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil 5 min, then drain, rinse off the gray foam and pat dry. This is optional, but it gives a cleaner, less greasy sauce.
Whisk all the braising sauce ingredients in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the ribs in batches, 2–3 min per side, until browned. Leave space between pieces so they brown instead of steam.
Put the carrots, daikon, onion and mushrooms in the slow cooker. Set the ribs on top and pour the sauce over everything.

Cover and cook on low 7–8 hr, until the meat pulls away from the bone and a fork slides in easily, but the pieces still hold together. If it still feels firm, cook 30–60 min more; short ribs only get more tender with time.
Gently lift the meat and vegetables onto a platter and tent with foil. Tilt the slow cooker and skim off the fat. There will be a lot, and a fat separator makes it easy.
Pour the liquid into a medium saucepan and simmer over medium heat 8–10 min, until glossy and slightly syrupy. For a thicker sauce, whisk in the cornstarch mixture and simmer 2 min more.
Spoon the sauce over the ribs and vegetables, top with green onions and sesame seeds, and serve with steamed short-grain rice.
tips: Best made a day ahead. Chill it overnight, lift off the hardened fat, and reheat gently on the stove or on low in the slow cooker.
Too sweet? Add a splash of rice vinegar or a squeeze of lemon. Too salty? Thin the sauce with water.
Serve with kimchi, a quick cucumber salad or garlicky sautéed spinach. Leftover sauce over rice with a fried egg makes a good lunch.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, stored in the sauce. Freezer up to 3 months; the daikon softens a little. Reheat covered over low heat with a splash of water until hot.
